newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams U.S. Radio Free Asia as interference.
newsitem.headline: China slams U.S. Radio Free Asia as interference.

text.p: Beijing on Tuesday told the United States to stop interfering with China's internal affairs through news transmissions by the infant Washington-funded broadcaster Radio Free Asia.
Radio Free Asia, which began broadcasts to China last month, would not help mend battered Sino-U.S. ties, Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing in Beijing.

Radio Free Asia's "key point is to use news methods to meddle in other countries' internal affairs", Shen said. "We think this action of the United States seriously violates the norms of international relations.

"It is not advantageous to the improvement and development of Sino-U.S. relations," he said, adding Washington should refrain from further interfering in China's affairs under the pretext of "news freedom".

Cross-Pacific ties have been sorely tested in recent years by disputes over trade, human rights, Taiwan and alleged nuclear proliferation by China, but both sides say relations have warmed recently after a series of high-level meetings.

U.S. commentators have speculated that Radio Free Asia will become a new thorn in ties between Beijing and Washington, particularly after U.S. congressmen successfully reversed a name-change to the less contentious Asia-Pacific Network.
The station is intended to promote democratic values by broadcasting local news to listeners in target countries in their own languages.
